image_description: A side-view digital rendering of a Triceratops dinosaur against a white background. The image focuses on the torso, hindquarters, and the rear portion of the frill. The head is partially visible on the right edge, showing the back of the frill and one brow horn. The forelimbs and head details are largely cut off by the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is mostly cropped out of the frame; only the rear of the skull/frill and the base of one horn are visible. The nasal horn and eye positioning cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout and beak area are completely outside the image frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible hindlimb is thick, columnar, and positioned vertically under the body, consistent with elephantine anatomy. The forelimb base also appears robust.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large, curved bony structure at the neck is clearly visible and matches the description of a ceratopsian frill.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible section of the frill shows a solid, textured surface with marginal ossifications (bumps) along the edge.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture displays a distinct pebbled/scaly pattern consistent with reptilian/dinosaurian reconstructions.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the hindlimb is fully visible, the forelimb is cut off at the shoulder/elbow, making a direct length comparison impossible within this crop.
The tail is not visible in the image; the frame ends at the hip/thigh region.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The transition from the lower leg to the foot lacks clear anatomical definition. The toes appear fused or melted into the ground contact point, lacking distinct digit separation expected in a high-fidelity render.
The connection between the visible forelimb stump and the torso appears slightly soft and ill-defined, suggesting a minor blending error where the limb meets the body mass.
